title: The Xbox Was Pitched to Microsoft as the DirectX Box
hook: In 1999 four Microsoft employees pitched a console built from PC parts and called it the DirectX Box. It launched on November 15, 2001 for $299, and this week it turned 25. What was your first original Xbox game?
script: Did you know the Xbox was pitched inside Microsoft as the DirectX Box? In 1999, four employees named Kevin Bachus, Seamus Blackley, Otto Berkes and Ted Hase pushed a bold idea. Microsoft should build a game console out of high end PC parts, running its own DirectX graphics technology. The working name was the DirectX Box, and the team soon shortened it to Xbox. Bill Gates unveiled the finished console at CES in Las Vegas on January 6, 2001, with The Rock beside him on stage. It went on sale in North America on November 15, 2001, for just under three hundred dollars. Nineteen games were available in its launch week. Inside was a 733 megahertz Intel processor, an Nvidia graphics chip, and sixty four megabytes of memory. It was also the first console to ship with a built in hard drive and an Ethernet port as standard. Microsoft sold one and a half million units in North America by the end of that year. Worldwide, it went on to sell more than 24 million consoles. This week the original Xbox celebrated its twenty fifth birthday. Microsoft marked it by adding twenty one more original Xbox games to PC. Did you own the original Xbox, and what was the first game you played on it? Follow for more gaming history.
